title: What is CSS specificity
question: What is CSS specificity and how does the browser use it to resolve conflicting styles?
realWorldScenario: When two CSS rules target the same element, specificity determines which one wins — understanding this prevents hours of debugging.

title: Specificity calculation
question: How is CSS specificity calculated? What are the four levels and how do inline styles, IDs, classes, and elements score?
realWorldScenario: Knowing that an ID selector (0,1,0,0) beats any number of class selectors (0,0,1,0) prevents specificity wars.

title: !important in CSS
question: What does `!important` do in CSS and why should you generally avoid it?
realWorldScenario: Overusing `!important` in third-party themes creates unmaintainable CSS that can only be overridden by more `!important` declarations.

title: CSS cascade rules
question: What is the CSS cascade? In what order does the browser resolve which style wins?
realWorldScenario: Origin (browser default < user < author < inline) → specificity → source order is the exact resolution chain.

title: CSS inheritance
question: What does CSS inheritance mean? Which properties are inherited by default and which are not?
realWorldScenario: Setting `font-family` on `body` applies to all text automatically because font properties are inherited.

title: CSS reset vs normalize
question: What is the difference between a CSS reset and normalize.css?
searchIntent: what is the difference between css reset and normalize
realWorldScenario: normalize.css preserves useful browser defaults and fixes inconsistencies; a hard reset strips everything to zero.

title: Pseudo-class specificity
question: What is the specificity of a pseudo-class like `:hover` and a pseudo-element like `::before`?
realWorldScenario: `:hover` counts as a class (0,0,1,0) while `::before` counts as an element (0,0,0,1).

title: Types of CSS selectors

realWorldScenario: Using the right selector type makes CSS more maintainable and avoids over-qualifying rules.
